Recreate encoded vectors from underlying values

Source: R/naxp_encoded.R
naxp_encoded.Rd

naxp_encoded() constructs a naxp_encoded vector from its underlying encoded values.

This is a specialised operation – normal practice is to use naxp_encode() to construct a naxp_encoded vector from text.

naxp_encoded() is exported so that encoded values previously extracted using as.integer() or as.numeric() and saved in a database or a file can be restored.

Usage

naxp_encoded(values, naxp)

Arguments

values

An integer or double vector of non-negative integers up to the naxp's maximum encoded value. NA is an error.

naxp

A naxp from naxp_parse(), a pattern string or a naxp_encoded vector, whose naxp is used.

Value

A naxp_encoded vector the same length as values. If the elements of values are named then the same names are applied to the elements of the returned vector.

Details

values must be non-negative integers up to the naxp's maximum encoded value, stored as either integer or double. NA is an error, because an encoded value is never NA: 0 means invalid text.

It is naxp, not the type of values, that decides how the values are stored:

  • integer if the naxp's maximum encoded value is less than \(2^{31}\), or

  • double if it is in the range \(2^{31}\) to \(2^{53}\).

If naxp has a maximum encoded value over \(2^{53}\) then an error is raised.

See also

naxp_encode() to create a naxp_encoded vector from text and a naxp.

naxp_encoded for working with a naxp_encoded vector.

Examples

postcode_naxp <- naxp_parse(r"(\9\9\9\9 \s!! \A\A)")

# Values saved earlier, such as a column read from a database
postcode_values <- c(684114L, 0L, 6760000L)

postcodes <- naxp_encoded(postcode_values, postcode_naxp)
postcodes
#> <naxp_encoded[3]> \9\9\9\9 \s!! \A\A
#> [1] 1012 AB       <invalid (0)> 9999 ZZ
